5.0.s.en: 1. The shaving of the prophet’s hair:

5.0.0.en: 1 “And thou, son of man, take thee a sharp knife, take thee a barber’s razor, and cause it to pass upon thine head and upon thy beard: then take thee balances to weigh, and divide the hair. 2 Thou shalt burn with fire a third part in the midst of the city, when the days of the siege are fulfilled: and thou shalt take a third part, and smite about it with a knife: and a third part thou shalt scatter in the wind; and I will draw out a sword after them. 3 Thou shalt also take thereof a few in number, and bind them in thy skirts. 4 Then take of them again, and cast them into the midst of the fire, and burn them in the fire; for thereof shall a fire come forth into all the house of Israel.”

5.0.1.en: “And thou, son of man, take thee a sharp knife, take thee a barber’s razor, and cause it to pass upon thine head and upon thy beard: then take thee balances to weigh, and divide the hair.

5.0.2.en: Thou shalt burn with fire a third part in the midst of the city, when the days of the siege are fulfilled: and thou shalt take a third part, and smite about it with a knife: and a third part thou shalt scatter in the wind” [1-2].

5.0.3.en: God commanded Moses to speak thus to the priests, the sons of Aaron: “They shall not make baldness upon their head, neither shall they shave off the corner of their beard, nor make any cuttings in their flesh. They shall be holy unto their God, and not profane the name of their God: for the offerings of the LORD made by fire, and the bread of their God, they do offer: therefore they shall be holy” (Lev 21:5-6). The divine commandment was clear and explicit that no razor should touch the head or beard of a priest, for he is holy to the Lord. For the hair left on a woman’s head is her adornment, but for a man it is a sign that he is not occupied with temporal matters, having consecrated every breath of his life to the priestly service. Therefore the command given to the prophet Ezekiel is a declaration of the defilement of the priests at that time, and of the Lord’s rejection of their sacrifices, their offerings and their prayers.

5.0.4.en: When the Lord wished in former times to save the people, the angel of the Lord appeared to the wife of Manoah, who was barren, and said to her: “For, lo, thou shalt conceive, and bear a son; and no razor shall come on his head: for the child shall be a Nazarite unto God from the womb: and he shall begin to deliver Israel out of the hand of the Philistines” (Judg 13:5). When this man’s hair was shaved off, the strength of the Lord departed from him and he became weak (Judg 16:17); indeed the Lord Himself departed from him (Judg 16:20), and he lost his eyes and was bound with fetters of brass, and became like an ox grinding in the prison house (Judg 16:21), and he was a mockery and a laughingstock to the pagans! But now it is God Himself who commands the shaving of the head and the beard, as a sign of His departure from the priests of His people, of their loss of spiritual sight, of their entering into captivity and of their becoming a laughingstock of the nations and the object of their derision.

5.0.5.en: The complete shaving of the hair signifies God’s refusal to enter into any relationship with them through the priests or the prophets; He accepts no offering and hears no prayer until He has disciplined them for their wickedness. It also signifies His rejection of His people because of their insistence on sin. If the Lord is the Head, then our life consists in abiding in Him. So the removal of the hair is the end of the people’s abiding in the source of their life. In this St. Jerome says: [The prophet Isaiah speaks of a sharp razor that shaves the head of sinners and the hair of their feet (Isa 7:20); he shaves his head as a type of Jerusalem, which had become a harlot (Ezek 5:1-5), a sign that everything in her had become insensible and life had been taken away from her.]

5.0.6.en: The complete shaving of the hair signifies intense grief, especially in the case of a death, and this was defilement in the eyes of the Lord. Therefore He warned His people, saying: “Ye are the children of the LORD your God: ye shall not cut yourselves, nor make any baldness between your eyes for the dead. For thou art holy unto the LORD thy God, and the LORD hath chosen thee to be a peculiar people unto himself” (Deut 14:1-2). But now Jerusalem had become as one reckoned among the dead. And since His people rejected Him, He commanded them, in the person of Ezekiel, to defile themselves by shaving the hair of their heads.

5.0.7.en: The shaving of the hair is also a sign of shame, humiliation and slavery. A man becomes without dignity, with no authority even over his own hair, whether to leave it or to shave it. For this reason the heads of slaves were shaved completely, and also those of kings when they were taken captive. This is what sin does to a man: it strips him of all authority and brings him down from the state of king and power to the shame of slavery, falling into captivity and humiliation. The servants of David were ashamed to meet their king because Hanun, king of the children of Ammon, suspected them and shaved off their beards, so they stayed at Jericho until their beards were grown, and then returned... Likewise a man cannot meet the Lord, his heavenly King, while he is in the shame and disgrace of sin; rather he waits until he declares his repentance, receives forgiveness and recovers his dignity, and so becomes able to meet God and all His heavenly and earthly hosts.

5.0.8.en: The shaving of the hair with a sharp knife signifies a bloody war, in which God allowed the hard-hearted Chaldeans to invade Judah, according to what His divine providence required. He allowed this because Judah had rebelled against God: a third would perish in the siege of Jerusalem, a third would be killed mercilessly by the sword at the hands of the soldiers of Nebuchadnezzar, and the remaining third would be scattered over the face of the earth among the peoples.

5.0.9.en: As for the weighing of the hair, it is a sign that what befalls the people of hunger, thirst, falling by the sword and scattering among the peoples does not take place randomly or by mere chance, but by divine ordering, and the Lord’s balances are just, faithful and exact.

5.0.10.en: “The LORD weigheth the hearts” (Prov 21:2) and the spirits (Prov 16:2); He before whose eyes are the ways of man, and “he pondereth all his goings” (Prov 5:21); who weighs the winds and weighs the waters by measure (Job 28:25), and comprehends the dust of the earth in a measure, and weighs the mountains in scales and the hills in a balance (Isa 40:12). His balances are true and just; He cannot bear deceit or partiality. This is the nature of God, which He desires to pour out into the lives of His children; therefore He often repeats the commandments: “Thou shalt not have in thy bag divers weights, a great and a small. Thou shalt not have in thine house divers measures, a great and a small. But thou shalt have a perfect and just weight, a perfect and just measure shalt thou have” (Deut 25:13-15); “Divers weights are an abomination unto the LORD; and a false balance is not good” (Prov 20:23); “A false balance is abomination to the LORD: but a just weight is his delight” (Prov 11:1). God weighs our lives and, sadly, finds them “in the balances they go up” (Ps 62:9), or as the wise Daniel said to King Belshazzar: “Thou art weighed in the balances, and art found wanting” (Dan 5:6). And now, what does the Lord do toward us, who have been found so? He bears the secret of our lack; He bears our iniquity upon Himself and comes forward to the balance, and behold, He is priced as a slave, He who is the Judge who judges the whole world. In bitterness He says: “So they weighed for my price thirty pieces of silver” (Zech 11:12). The Lord is valued as a slave, while the slave stands in his self-righteousness to say: “Let me be weighed in an even balance, that God may know mine integrity” (Job 31:6). The Perfect One was weighed, bearing our lack, and came under shame, while man in the pride of his heart wishes to be justified in the balances before God.

5.0.11.en: In any case, Ezekiel’s hair was weighed as a symbol of the people fallen under the weight of sin, and found deserving of hunger, thirst, the sword and scattering... These are the fruits of uncleanness and evil.

5.0.12.en: Although the people were found wanting in the balance, God does not forget the very few among them, those who, because of their faithfulness to Him and their obedience to His words, He keeps in the skirt of His garment, under His care. This remnant perhaps refers to the remnant that was left in Jerusalem under the leadership of Gedaliah. And perhaps it refers to the remnant that remains faithful to the Lord in the days of the false prophet or the Antichrist. They are the hidden company of the Lord, kept and concealed in Him; He knows them by name and puts a hedge around them so that none of them is lost, and the wicked enemy does not snatch them away. But sadly, the Lord commanded that a few of this small number be burned, because after entering under His care they rejected Him. Of these the Apostle said that they began in the Spirit but are being made perfect by the flesh (Gal 3:3). Therefore the Lord instructs us to endure to the end (Mt 10:12), and warns us of the last days, when it is feared that even the elect may be deceived (Mt 24:24).

5.1.0.en: 5 “Thus saith the Lord GOD; This is Jerusalem: I have set it in the midst of the nations and countries that are round about her. 6 And she hath changed my judgments into wickedness more than the nations, and my statutes more than the countries that are round about her: for they have refused my judgments and my statutes, they have not walked in them. 7 Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD; Because ye multiplied more than the nations that are round about you, and have not walked in my statutes, neither have kept my judgments, neither have done according to the judgments of the nations that are round about you,” God, like a father disciplining his children, reveals to them the secret of their punishment. He is not a tyrannical master nor an avenger; rather, even in the severity of His discipline He desires our return and repentance... Therefore He shows us our weaknesses so that we may abandon them.

5.2.0.en: Two things grieve the heart of God: the broken commandment and the defiled temple. Concerning the commandment He says: “For they have refused my judgments and my statutes, they have not walked in them” [6]. And it is strange that when the believer falls into disobedience he becomes more wicked than the unbeliever, for the Lord says: “She hath changed my judgments into wickedness more than the nations” [6]. As for the defiling of the temple, He says: “Surely, because thou hast defiled my sanctuary with all thy detestable things, and with all thine abominations, therefore will I also diminish thee; neither shall mine eye spare, neither will I have any pity” [11].

5.2.1.en: The keeping of the commandment and worship (the temple) are two things that go together and are joined in the life of the believer. By obeying the commandment we gain boldness to stand before God, and standing before Him in worship supports our life in obedience to the commandment. Whoever thinks that he keeps the commandment apart from the spirit of worship deceives himself, and so does whoever thinks that he pleases the Lord by worship without walking in obedience to the commandment.

5.3.0.en: 8 “Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD; Behold, I, even I, am against thee, and will execute judgments in the midst of thee in the sight of the nations.” When He sent to the people of Judah the prophet Jeremiah to rebuke them for their sins, He said to him: “Go and cry in the ears of Jerusalem” (Jer 2:1), as though He wished to whisper in their ears so that they might repent without anyone knowing what they had done; but when they did not listen, He asked him to stand in the gate of the house of the Lord and proclaim the word of rebuke (Jer 7:1), and when they still did not listen, He was compelled to make His chastisements of His people public before all the nations. They sinned openly without shame, and He tried to correct them without wounding their feelings, but in the face of their growing arrogance He says: “I will execute judgments in the midst of thee in the sight of the nations” [8], “Moreover I will make thee waste, and a reproach among the nations that are round about thee, in the sight of all that pass by. So it shall be a reproach and a taunt, an instruction and an astonishment unto the nations that are round about thee” [14-15].

5.3.1.en: Jerusalem became a lesson to the nations around her, and a visible lesson to the whole world. For the holy God does not accept sin, nor does He make peace with it, even if His people commit it in the holy city!

5.3.2.en: God, as the Lover of mankind, covers our sins and weaknesses once and many times, but when He finds our healing in exposing us, He announces His severe chastisements upon us. This is also what the Church does with her children and servants: she heals with love and covers, but if the matter calls for public discipline she does not refrain, for the sake of the salvation of her children. In the apostolic age the Apostle judged publicly the one who fell into sin with his father’s wife, saying: “It is reported commonly that there is fornication among you, and such fornication as is not so much as named among the Gentiles, that one should have his father’s wife... For I verily, as absent in body, but present in spirit, have judged already, as though I were present, concerning him that hath so done this deed, In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, when ye are gathered together, and my spirit, with the power of our Lord Jesus Christ, To deliver such an one unto Satan for the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord Jesus... Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened” (1 Cor 5:1-7).

5.4.0.en: 9 “And I will do in thee that which I have not done, and whereunto I will not do any more the like, because of all thine abominations. 10 Therefore the fathers shall eat the sons in the midst of thee, and the sons shall eat their fathers; and I will execute judgments in thee, and the whole remnant of thee will I scatter into all the winds. 11 Wherefore, as I live, saith the Lord GOD; Surely, because thou hast defiled my sanctuary with all thy detestable things, and with all thine abominations, therefore will I also diminish thee; neither shall mine eye spare, neither will I have any pity. 12 A third part of thee shall die with the pestilence, and with famine shall they be consumed in the midst of thee: and a third part shall fall by the sword round about thee; and I will scatter a third part into all the winds, and I will draw out a sword after them.”

5.4.1.en: They vied with one another in evil and surpassed the nations; therefore God also disciplines them with unique chastisements: “And I will do in thee that which I have not done, and whereunto I will not do any more the like, because of all thine abominations. Therefore the fathers shall eat the sons in the midst of thee, and the sons shall eat their fathers; and I will execute judgments in thee, and the whole remnant of thee will I scatter into all the winds” [9-10].

5.4.2.en: This is the bitterest punishment under which believers can fall: that one of them eats the other, indeed that the father eats his son and the son his father! For when the grace of God abandons them, corruption creeps into them from within, and through divisions and schisms one member eats another, even if he is bound to him by ties of flesh or of spirit, and finally nothing is left of them except ashes that the Lord scatters into every wind!

5.4.3.en: I say that the fruit of sin is that the community eats one another instead of supporting one another; indeed division creeps into the man himself, so that he rises up against himself, loses his peace, his balance and his vitality, and the man, because of sin, becomes like ashes of no value, scattered by the winds in every direction!

5.5.0.en: 13 “Thus shall mine anger be accomplished, and I will cause my fury to rest upon them, and I will be comforted: and they shall know that I the LORD have spoken it in my zeal, when I have accomplished my fury in them. 14 Moreover I will make thee waste, and a reproach among the nations that are round about thee, in the sight of all that pass by. 15 So it shall be a reproach and a taunt, an instruction and an astonishment unto the nations that are round about thee, when I shall execute judgments in thee in anger and in fury and in furious rebukes. I the LORD have spoken it.”

5.6.0.en: The Lord assured Judah that this unique public chastisement does not come from the prophet, who is not speaking against them, but from God Himself: “I the LORD have spoken it” [15].

5.6.1.en: Although the Chaldeans fight against you and take your people captive, in truth they are an instrument in the hand of God, who raises the nations against His people to discipline them. Therefore He affirms: “Behold, I, even I, am against thee” [9], repeating the phrase “I the LORD have spoken it” and the like about 14 times in this book.

5.6.2.en: For this reason, when Absalom rose up against his father David and the latter fled, Shimei the son of Gera came out against him, cursing and casting stones at David, and all the servants of the king, and the people and the mighty men around him; then Abishai said to the king: “Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? let me go over, I pray thee, and take off his head” (2 Sam 16:9). But David, in wisdom and humility, said: “Let him curse, because the LORD hath said unto him, Curse David. Who shall then say, Wherefore hast thou done so?... It may be that the LORD will look on mine affliction, and that the LORD will requite me good for his cursing this day.” St. John Chrysostom sees in the plots of others against us an opportunity for repentance, for he says: [If we sin, God raises our enemies against us to discipline us. Therefore it is fitting for us not to fight them, but to examine ourselves and instruct ourselves. Let us accept sufferings as we accept medicines from the physician for our salvation, and as we accept discipline from a father, so that we may be glorified.]

5.7.0.en: 16 “When I shall send upon them the evil arrows of famine, which shall be for their destruction, and which I will send to destroy you: and I will increase the famine upon you, and will break your staff of bread: 17 So will I send upon you famine and evil beasts, and they shall bereave thee; and pestilence and blood shall pass through thee; and I will bring the sword upon thee. I the LORD have spoken it.”

5.7.1.en: In His longsuffering and love, God began with secret speaking to His people, then with open speaking, and finally was compelled to open chastisement; and here too He disciplines in stages, that perhaps they may repent and He may remove the pain from them. He allows them to hunger, then increases His pressure upon them until they are in need of bread. And when they do not return, He stirs up the wild beasts against them to devour their children, then He allows pestilence and the shedding of blood... He seeks not vengeance but repentance, by every way.

5.7.2.en: Establish me in You, O tender Disciplinarian!

5.7.3.en: * Establish me in You, O tender Disciplinarian!

5.7.4.en: You allowed Your prophet Ezekiel to shave off all the hair of his head, to declare Your intense grief over the corruption of Your people as though they were dead, and to threaten Your people that You would remove them from You as hair from the head, and to reject their priesthood, which had become defiled, and to assure them that they live as captive slaves with shaven heads!

5.7.5.en: * Discipline me... but do not hand me over to another than You!

5.7.6.en: For You are the tender Disciplinarian!

5.7.7.en: * You disciplined me in secret and I was not restrained; behold, You expose me among my people, indeed even among the nations...

5.7.8.en: Let it be... but do not deprive me of Your salvation!

5.7.9.en: For You are the tender Disciplinarian!
